questions.q: What was Loung Ung's life like before the Khmer Rouge took power?
a: She had a comfortable city life because her father was a military official
She lived in a rural village and worked in the fields each day
She had already fled Cambodia and grown up as a refugee
She lived in an orphanage after her parents were killed
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes a middle-class apartment in Phnom Penh and schooling for the children.

questions.q: Why did the family have to hide who they were?
a: Her father's status and her mother's Chinese heritage made them targets
They had openly supported the previous government in public
They refused to hand over their property to the new regime
They were suspected of spying for a foreign country
questions.why: Lesson 1 says both the father's position and the mother's mixed background endangered them.

questions.q: What happened to the city workers sent to rural labor camps?
a: Two-thirds died of starvation or illness within five months
Most were released once they learned farming skills
They were given extra rations to keep them working
They were moved into new homes and paid in rice
questions.why: Lesson 2 says educated city people were treated as the lowest class and starved.

questions.q: How did Loung's brother help the family survive?
a: He worked at the village chief's house and smuggled scraps home
He traded the family's jewelry for a supply of rice
He joined the Khmer Rouge and shared his rations
He led the family into the jungle to live off the land
questions.why: Lesson 2 says he endured beatings so he could bring leftover food to his siblings.

questions.q: Why did Loung's mother send her children away?
a: So they could pose as orphans and escape being traced and killed
So they could find work and send money back to her
So they could join relatives who had already left Cambodia
So they could receive an education in another city
questions.why: Lesson 3 says she knew the regime would soon execute the rest of the family.
